The commit body MUST document the search (which DOI/publisher/archive was queried + return shape — e.g., "searched ACM DOI 10.1145/<doi> 2026-05-05 — paywall-only, no excerpt found; searched Internet Archive — no scan; searched publisher excerpt page — none"). Mere preference is INSUFFICIENT — if any auditable surrogate exists (DOI/PDF/excerpt/scan), use it as the normative source instead of the physical-only book cite. e.g., ACM DOI `https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/<doi>` for ACM papers IS auditable when paywall-free. docs\sota-architecture-audit\future-evolution\_extension-and-reaudit-metadata.json:475:    "readme_head_2000": "# Superpowers\n\nSuperpowers is a complete software development methodology for your coding agents, built on top of a set of composable skills and some initial instructions that make sure your agent uses them.\n\n## Quickstart\n\nGive your agent Superpowers: [Claude Code](#claude-code), [Codex CLI](#codex-cli), [Codex App](#codex-app), [Factory Droid](#factory-droid), [Gemini CLI](#gemini-cli), [OpenCode](#opencode), [Cursor](#cursor), [GitHub Copilot CLI](#github-copilot-cli).\n\n## How it works\n\nIt starts from the moment you fire up your coding agent. As soon as it sees that you're building something, it *doesn't* just jump into trying to write code. Instead, it steps back and asks you what you're really trying to do. \n\nOnce it's teased a spec out of the conversation, it shows it to you in chunks short enough to actually read and digest. \n\nAfter you've signed off on the design, your agent puts together an implementation plan that's clear enough for an enthusiastic junior engineer with poor taste, no judgement, no project context, and an aversion to testing to follow. It emphasizes true red/green TDD, YAGNI (You Aren't Gonna Need It), and DRY. \n\nNext up, once you say \"go\", it launches a *subagent-driven-development* process, having agents work through each engineering task, inspecting and reviewing their work, and continuing forward. It's not uncommon for Claude to be able to work autonomously for a couple hours at a time without deviating from the plan you put together.\n\nThere's a bunch more to it, but that's the core of the system. And because the skills trigger automatically, you don't need to do anything special. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). Use for SHARED JSONL log targets (`mcp_health.jsonl`, `subagent_transcripts.jsonl`, `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` class) where consumers expect interleaved appends from multiple writers and unified-view semantics are required.

After every `os.open`, the caller MUST: (i) read `current_mode = stat.S_IMODE(os.fstat(fd).st_mode)`; (ii) if `current_mode != mode` AND the file is owned by caller-uid, call `os.fchmod(fd, mode)` to coerce existing file to the mode invariant; (iii) if `os.fchmod` raises (`PermissionError` due to read-only mount, alien owner, ACL conflict on Windows NTFS, etc.), FAIL CLOSED — propagate the exception rather than proceeding with non-conforming perms (the audit-trail invariant is enforced everywhere or fails loudly). Document in commit body for any consumer applying this rule: one-time migration shell command `find .claude/state -name '*.jsonl' -perm /044 -exec chmod 0600 {} +` (POSIX) OR `Get-ChildItem -Path .claude/state -Filter *.jsonl -Recurse | Where-Object { ($_ | Get-Acl).AccessToString -match 'Everyone Allow Read' } | ForEach-Object { icacls $_.FullName /inheritance:r /grant ${env:USERNAME}:F }` (Windows) for legacy `mcp_health.jsonl` / `subagent_transcripts.jsonl` / `codex_postcommit_reviews.jsonl` / `subagent_start.jsonl` / `worktree_lifecycle_audit.jsonl` files created at `0o644` per pre-Round-6 mandates. The `O_CREAT` flag ensures a missing log auto-creates rather than failing the first writer; **if `os.open` raises (read-only mount, permission denied, disk full), the exception MUST propagate — do not catch-and-ignore** (per Round-5 F-1 silent-failure finding). Take an **exclusive advisory lock** (`fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` on POSIX / `msvcrt.locking` on Windows); **if neither primitive is available, or if the platform does not enforce advisory locks (e.g., NFS without NLM support), FAIL CLOSED — raise rather than proceeding without a lock** (per Round-5 F-2 NFS-silent-succeed finding). **Windows separate-lockfile mechanism** *(Round-7c per T3 round-7b NEEDS-ATTENTION conf=0.78 NEW-CLASS finding on commit `48c49fb` caught by codex GPT-5.5 BRIDGE-MODE)*: `msvcrt.locking` locks `nbytes` from CURRENT file-pointer position, NOT the whole file like POSIX `fcntl.flock`. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Module returns `lock_fd` for Windows callers to release; `None` for POSIX. **Lock-protocol rollout constraint** *(Round-7c per same T3 finding)*: when the lock protocol bumps (direct-jsonl-fd → separate-lockfile-v1, or separate-lockfile-v1 → separate-lockfile-v2-versioned), enforce single-version deployment for the entire concurrent-writer cohort. Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Currently sss has ZERO consumers of `_atomic_jsonl_append.py` (FORWARD-REF wire-up Ships 2-5 pending per `tmp/wave22-orchestrator-salvage-jsonl-mode-bits-audit-2026-05-05.md`), so the version-skew window is THEORETICAL until first hook migrates to use the module. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). After the write, `os.fsync(fd)` if durability is part of the contract (audit-trail JSONL needs fsync; ephemeral telemetry may skip); **if `os.fsync` raises (`EIO`, `ENOSPC`), propagate the exception — do not silently ignore a durability failure when durability is contracted** (per Round-5 F-4 fsync-failure finding). Go to [Settings > Capabilities](https://claude.ai/settings/capabilities)\n2. Enable Skills toggle\n3. Browse available skills or upload custom skills\n4. **For Team/Enterprise**: Admin must enable Skills organization-wide first\n\n### Claude Code CLI\n\n```bash\n# Install skills from marketplace\n/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills\n\n# Or install from local directory\n/plugin add /path/to/skill-directory\n```\n\n### Claude API\n\nSkills are accessible via the `/v1/skills` API endpoint. Under O_APPEND the JSONL fd's pointer moves on each write, breaking lock-release symmetry (LK_UNLCK at the new pointer would find no lock at the byte LK_LOCK was issued for). Round-7b workaround (shipped at `scripts/_atomic_jsonl_append.py:_acquire_lock(fd, path)` commit `48c49fb`): open separate `<jsonl-path>.lock` file with 1-byte placeholder + lock byte 0 of the LOCKFILE (no writes to lockfile means file pointer stays at byte 0). Old + new code locking DIFFERENT lock domains do NOT mutually exclude — concurrent writers can race even though each ALONE acquires its lock correctly. Mitigations (pick ONE before any concurrent rollout): **(i) transitional dual-lock**: acquire both old AND new protocol locks in series during the transition window; **(ii) runtime version-marker**: write protocol-version byte to lockfile + fail-closed on read-version-mismatch (FORWARD-REF for v2 lock protocol bump); **(iii) single-version cohort barrier**: coordinate cohort upgrade via deployment system before any new-version runs. Future protocol bumps MUST honor one of (i)/(ii)/(iii). HOLD the lock across BOTH (a) JSON-encoding the record AND (b) the single low-level `os.write(fd, encoded_bytes)` — never use buffered text writes (`f.write(json.dumps(rec) + "\n")` via Python file objects can split into multiple writes). **If JSON encoding raises (`UnicodeEncodeError`, non-serializable type), release the lock and propagate the exception — do not silently drop the record** (per Round-5 F-3 silent-record-drop finding). For records where **`len(encoded_bytes)` — the byte count AFTER JSON encoding, NOT the key count of the dict —** exceeds the platform atomic-write bound (≤PIPE_BUF 4KB POSIX; ≤512 bytes for Windows or treat the lock as the sole correctness boundary), reject the record OR shard via option (b) filename-namespace; do NOT silently truncate (per Round-5 F-5 measurement-target finding). 94:- [License](#license)
98:Claude Skills are reusable instruction packages that teach an AI agent how to handle a specific class of tasks. Each skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter (name, description) and Markdown instructions, optionally bundled with scripts, references, and assets. Anthropic introduced the format in October 2025 and released it as an [open standard](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) in December 2025; it's now supported by Claude Code, Claude.ai, the Claude API, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and Windsurf.
100:Skills load progressively. At session start, the agent sees only each skill's name and description — roughly 100 tokens per skill. The full SKILL.md body (typically under 5,000 tokens) loads only when the agent decides the skill is relevant to the current task. Auxiliary files in `scripts/` and `references/` load on demand. This is what lets a single agent host hundreds of skills without bloating its context window.
102:Skills are not MCP servers and not tools. MCP defines how an agent connects to external systems — auth, transport, tool discovery. Tools are the individual functions an agent invokes. Skills define the workflow — what to do, in what order, with what guardrails — once the agent has the connections and tools it needs. In production, all three layers run together: MCP for access, tools for actions, skills for behavior.

## Quickstart: Connect Claude to 500+ Apps

The **connect-apps** plugin lets Claude perform real actions - send emails, create issues, post to Slack. It handles auth and connects to 500+ apps using Composio under the hood.

### 1. Install the Plugin

```bash
claude --plugin-dir ./connect-apps-plugin
```

### 2. Run Setup

```
/connect-apps:setup
```

Paste your API key when asked. (Get a free key at [dashboard.composio.dev](https://dashboard.composio.dev/login?utm_source=Github&utm_content=AwesomeSkills))

### 3. Restart & Try It

```bash
exit
claude
```

If you receive the email, Claude is now connected to 500+ apps.

## What Are Claude Skills?

Claude Skills are reusable instruction packages that teach an AI agent how to handle a specific class of tasks. Each skill is a folder containing a `SKILL.md` file with YAML frontmatter (name, description) and Markdown instructions, optionally bundled with scripts, references, and assets. Anthropic introduced the format in October 2025 and released it as an [open standard](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) in December 2025; it's now supported by Claude Code, Claude.ai, the Claude API, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, and Windsurf.

Skills load progressively. At session start, the agent sees only each skill's name and description — roughly 100 tokens per skill. The full SKILL.md body (typically under 5,000 tokens) loads only when the agent decides the skill is relevant to the current task. Auxiliary files in `scripts/` and `references/` load on demand. This is what lets a single agent host hundreds of skills without bloating its context window.

Skills are not MCP servers and not tools. MCP defines how an agent connects to external systems — auth, transport, tool discovery. Tools are the individual functions an agent invokes. Skills define the workflow — what to do, in what order, with what guardrails — once the agent has the connections and tools it needs. In production, all three layers run together: MCP for access, tools for actions, skills for behavior.

## 💡 Why this exists

You shouldn't have to rebuild the same RAG pipeline, agent loop, or MCP integration from scratch every time you start a new LLM project.

**Awesome LLM Apps is a cookbook of ready-to-run templates** - starter code you can fork, customize, and ship as a production LLM app. Every template here is self-contained with full source code, not collected from elsewhere.

- 🛠️ **Hand-built, not curated** - every template is original work, tested end-to-end before it ships.
- 🧪 **Runs in 3 commands** - no broken `requirements.txt`, no "figure it out yourself" scaffolding.
- 🧠 **Covers the modern AI stack** - AI Agents, Multi-agent Teams, MCP Agents, Voice AI Agents, RAG, Agent Skills, Fine-tuning.
- 🌐 **Provider-agnostic** - switch between Claude, Gemini, GPT, Llama, Qwen, xAI and others with a config change.
- 📚 **Step-by-step tutorials** - every featured template has a free walkthrough on [Unwind AI](https://www.theunwindai.com).
- 💸 **Apache-2.0** - fork it, ship it, sell it. No paywall, no signup, no telemetry.

> ⭐ **If this saves you time, [star the repo](https://github.com/Shubhamsaboo/awesome-llm-apps/stargazers) - that's how the next developer discovers it.**

## 🚀 Quick Start

Run your first agent in **30 seconds**:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Shubhamsaboo/awesome-llm-apps.git
cd awesome-llm-apps/starter_ai_agents/ai_travel_agent
pip install -r requirements.txt
streamlit run travel_agent.py
```

### Step 4 - Apply LOAD-BEARING 5-row bar (Rider 4)

Per candidate, fill the table:

| Row | Criterion | Result | Evidence (FILE:LINE or URL) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. T1 source | Primary-source verifiable | PASS/FAIL | repo URL + sha or file:line |
| 2. Numeric | Measurable improvement over current | PASS/FAIL/[UNKNOWN] | benchmark number, not just star count |
| 3. Alternatives dismissed | >=2 candidates surveyed + reason rejected | PASS/FAIL | named alternatives + rejection reason |
| 4. Practitioner endorsement | Named user shipping at scale | PASS/FAIL/[UNKNOWN] | citation to Karpathy/Boris/Simon/etc. for OUR use case (not generic) |
| 5. Verdict | ADOPT/STUDY-PILOT/REJECT | (computed) | any [UNKNOWN] auto-downgrades to STUDY |

ALL 5 GREEN -> ADOPT-NOW. Any [UNKNOWN] -> STUDY-PILOT. Any FAIL -> REJECT.

### Step 4.5 - Probe 1-6 harness-fit verification (REQUIRED post-PASS, Axis-4 of convergence-gate)

**The 5-row bar above is necessary BUT NOT SUFFICIENT.** Per `.claude/rules/agent-harness-fit-verification.md` (n=9 promotion-source ladder + FM-09 codex-rescue blind-spot specialization at n=5/5 same-arc 100% base rate), candidates that PASS the 5-row bar STILL routinely fail at ship-target verification because of architectural mismatch invisible to upstream-source audit. Apply the 6-probe DAG BEFORE writing the T1 consult prompt OR queuing the ship:

- **Probe 1 — count-OVER**: verify agent-claimed counts (commits / files / stars) against authoritative LOCAL source (`git log`, `wc -l`, `Glob | wc -l`, fresh `mcp__github__search_repositories` star refresh). Agent counts via remote APIs drift, paginate-truncate, or include stale cache.
- **Probe 2 — SDK-vs-CLI surface**: verify the candidate's invocation surface exists in claude-sota's actual hooks/scripts/.claude/settings.json. Does claude-sota use the SDK or CLI? Does the candidate's mechanism map to claude-sota's actual mode (interactive vs print-mode vs SDK-managed-agent)? If candidate requires a mode claude-sota doesn't run in, REJECT-for-fit even if SOTA-valid upstream.
- **Probe 3 — architectural-API**: verify API-ecosystem match (Anthropic-API vs OpenAI-API vs vendor-neutral OTel). claude-sota's gpt5.5/codex hooks talk to OpenAI-API endpoints; Anthropic-only primitives (e.g., `cache_control`) don't apply there.
- **Probe 4 — plugin-namespace (CRITICAL)**: check the available-skills list for `everything-claude-code:<artifact>` / `codex:<artifact>` / `<plugin>:<artifact>` BEFORE recommending vendoring of upstream artifact. If plugin already exposes the artifact, REJECT-for-fit per `.claude/rules/kiss-dry-yagni.md` Must-Never #4 (no duplicate functionality), even if convergence-gate Axis 1+2+3 PASS.
- **Probe 5 — mode-harness-shape**: cross-check candidate's operational mode against claude-sota's autonomous /loop mode. HARD-GATE-on-user-interaction skills are incompatible with autonomous mode. Meta-skills assuming sister-harness presence (e.g., Superpowers TDD-for-skills) REJECT-for-fit if local sister-harness absent. Verbatim ports introducing 7+ files when sibling skills are 1-3 files = size-sprawl REJECT-for-fit.
- **Probe 6 — direct-file/registry blockers (FM-09 promotion iter-67)**: for adoption candidates whose viability depends on upstream artifact existence + license-compatibility, run direct-file/registry probes. LICENSE file read at upstream root (REJECT if AGPLv3/GPLv3/SSPL/proprietary; PASS if MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/ISC/MPL-2.0). README badge inspection (archive-status, deprecation, "moved to maintenance mode"). Registry direct-existence probe (`curl https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>` / `curl https://pypi.org/pypi/<pkg>/json` — `{"error":"Not found"}` / 404 = phantom). Build-deps availability (`which cargo gcc clang`).

**Codex-rescue blind-spot specialization (FM-09 n=5 same-arc 2026-05-02)**: codex-rescue (GPT-5.5 deep-dive variant) systematically returns ADOPT-NOW / STUDY-PILOT verdicts WITHOUT running Probe 4 / Probe 5 / Probe 6 — pattern is agent-architecture-specific (specializes in abstract-pattern reasoning, NOT repo-local-inventory reasoning). When receiving a codex-rescue ADOPT-NOW / STUDY-PILOT verdict on awesome-agentic-patterns / SOTA-catalog abstract-pattern candidates, **MUST spawn 2nd-stage harness-fit-aware agent** (`sota-researcher` / `architect` / `Explore` — NOT codex-rescue intermediary which has the same blind-spot) with explicit Probe 4+5+6 mandate. 2nd-stage verdict OVERRIDES first-stage if any probe fails. n=5 base rate = 100% override on observable cases.

If ANY probe surfaces a blocker, REJECT-FOR-FIT even if all 5 LOAD-BEARING bar rows GREEN. The blocker is STRUCTURAL — no operational mitigation exists. HONEST-NON-FINDING per `.claude/rules/synthesis-layer-verify.md §Reporting categories` is high-value output (saves downstream T1+T2+ship+revert cycles).

### Step 5 - Self-test BEFORE commit (Rider 4 + 6)

Before any ship:
- [ ] Did I run >=3 distinct search tool types? (exa + github + deepwiki minimum)
- [ ] Did I name >=2 dismissed alternatives WITH reason?
- [ ] Did I verify the most load-bearing claim against primary source? (Don't accept "X is endorsed by Y" without grepping Y's public artifacts)
- [ ] Did I ask "is the category itself correct?" before "which option in the category?"
- [ ] **Rider 6**: did I sanity-check my measurement tools? (broad grep >= narrow grep, 2 patterns >= 1, 2 reviewers >= 1)
- [ ] **Rider 5**: did I disambiguate user category before audit?
